message.content:
Civil law, also known as civil jurisprudence or civil law system, is a legal framework that governs non-criminal disputes between private parties. Its components can be broadly categorized into several key areas: | Component | Description | |-----------|-------------| | **Legal Sources** | • **Statutes & Codes** – Written laws enacted by legislatures (e.g., Civil Code, Commercial Code).
• **Case Law / Judicial Precedent** – Decisions from higher courts that guide lower courts.
• **Customary Law** – Long‑standing practices recognized as binding. | | **Branches of Civil Law** | • **Contract Law** – Rules governing agreements and obligations.
• **Tort Law** – Liability for wrongful acts causing harm.
• **Property Law** – Rights and duties related to real and personal property.
• **Family Law** – Marriage, divorce, child custody, adoption.
• **Succession/Inheritance Law** – Distribution of estates after death. | | **Procedural Elements** | • **Jurisdiction** – Which court has authority over a case.
• **Venue** – Physical location where a case is heard.
• **Pleadings** – Formal documents (complaint, answer, counterclaim).
• **Discovery** – Exchange of evidence and information.
• **Trial & Judgment** – Presentation of evidence, decision by judge/jury. | | **Remedies** | • **Damages** – Monetary compensation.
• **Specific Performance** – Court order to fulfill contractual obligations.
• **Injunctions** – Orders to prevent or compel actions.
• **Restitution** – Return of property or money. | | **Legal Principles** | • **Good Faith & Fair Dealing** – Parties must act honestly.
• **Equitable Remedies** – Courts may grant non-monetary relief.
• **Doctrine of Unjust Enrichment** – Prevents one party from benefiting at another’s expense. | | **Institutions** | • **Courts** – Trial courts, appellate courts, supreme courts.
• **Legal Professionals** – Lawyers, judges, notaries.
• **Regulatory Bodies** – Bar associations, professional licensing boards. | These components interact to form a comprehensive system that resolves disputes, protects rights, and ensures fairness in civil matters.
